name: Kosi River — Kusaha Embankment Breach (2008 Bihar Flood)
description: Real-world dam-break-analogue case study: on 18 Aug 2008 the eastern afflux embankment of the Kosi River, ~12 km upstream of Kosi Barrage, breached near Kusaha (Sunsari district, Nepal). The river avulsed onto an old channel and inundated ~3700 sq km across five North Bihar districts. Used here as the reference breach scenario for both the SPH surge model and the SWE flood-spread model.

river.name: Kosi (Koshi) River
river.basin: Kosi Basin, sub-basin of the Ganga

structure.note: Not a storage dam — the Kosi system is a barrage (diversion weir) with flanking flood-control embankments (afflux bunds). The 2008 disaster was a breach of the eastern embankment, not the barrage structure itself.

barrage.name: Kosi Barrage (Bhimnagar Barrage)
barrage.location: Bhimnagar, Sunsari district, Nepal / Supaul district border, Bihar, India

breach_site.name: Kusaha (Kasuha) eastern afflux embankment breach
breach_site.coordinates_note: Approximate — derived from the nearest mapped settlement (Paschim Kasuha, Sunsari district); no surveyed breach-point coordinates were found in public sources. Verify against a topo sheet or satellite imagery before using for precision hydraulic siting.

breach_event.cause: Heavy monsoon flow combined with poor embankment maintenance; warnings were not acted on in time.

simulation_defaults.breach_width_note: Not documented in public sources for the 2008 event — set to a plausible order-of-magnitude default for a major afflux-embankment failure. Treat as a tunable scenario parameter, not a historical fact.
simulation_defaults.breach_hydrograph_note: No time-resolved historical hydrograph for the 2008 Kusaha breach is publicly documented (the event unfolded over days, not the few-hour window this demo simulates). The solver assumes a linear ramp from 0 to breach_event.discharge_at_breach_cumecs over this many minutes, then holds at peak — a standard simplified breach hydrograph shape, not a historical fact.
simulation_defaults.peak_discharge_note: Uses the barrage's design peak discharge as an upper-bound scenario; the actual 2008 breach discharge (3675 cumecs, see breach_event) is the better value for reproducing that specific historical event.

aoi_bounds.note: Bounding box used for the DEM, population raster, and satellite layers in this case study — covers the breach site down through Kosi Barrage into the upper Bihar flood corridor. Does not cover the full historical 3700 sq km extent (which reaches further south/east to Purnia); scoped for demo tractability.
